note:
v1 92.522/92.512. THE TRITONE QUESTION: afro-tinged minimal house, 119 -> 119.5 bpm, B minor.
- The hook is the TRITONE PARADOX: Shepard-tone pairs a tritone apart, B-F first, then each stair step with its tritone (B-F, C#-G, D-G#, F#-C). The stair climbs, but every step has no up or down.
- A voice asks it aloud once the seam has passed: "up... or down?", answering t3's "one more step up".
- A 12/8 bell and triplet tom pickups over the four on the floor; triplet shakers, sixteenths at the peak; a clap a triplet late.
- The machine boom as a bass line on B; a sparse Bm9 dub stab in an echo room.
- A kickless break with the question slowed.
- SEAMS: in, a BASS SWAP: t4's first 16 bars have a high-passed kick so t3 keeps the low end, and its shakers and hats sit under t3's phrase. Out: kick, hats and a held B1 for t5's 808 (mixplan rows filled).
-11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 1. (Not queued.)
next: Rhythm (57: the triplets read as on-grid); ears on the pairs' level.

note: v2 91.021/90.999 (kept on judgment over v1 92.666 rescored). UNSWAPPED (T4_R2): the composed bass swap is gone. In the mix's linear 16-bar crossfade, v1's high-passed kick under t3's tail sagged the sub (<120 Hz, per bar) to -25 dB, then jumped: an 11.1 dB range across the overlap. Unswapped it is 5.1 dB on the linear fade and 4.7 dB with the mixer's swap at the midpoint, so mixplan t3>t4 swap = mid. compscore's spectrum and flow liked the thin head (-1.6); the mix does not. Beat drift 0 ms. -11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 1. (Not queued.)
next: Rhythm (triplets read on-grid); t4>t5 sub step (t5's head is ~7 dB under t4's sub; the swap does not help there).

v3 91.034/89.974 (v2 rescored 90.369/90.349). THE QUESTION ANSWERED IN RHYTHM (T4_R3), after chirper-one's and chirper-three's notes that t11 also features the tritone paradox. t4 now leads with what only it has:
- In A2 and B2 the voice asks "up... or down?" every eight bars, and the toms ANSWER in the next bar: a rising triplet on the one, a falling triplet on the three. Both answers.
- A low tom on the dotted quarters puts three against the four (a three-bar cycle) under the 12/8 bell, which comes up 3 dB.
- The Shepard pairs drop back to colour: every other bar, 4 dB down.
